scenario: A mobility-investor memo highlights only bike-share operators that survive expansion and keep fleet utilization above 75%. Investors use the highlighted average utilization to infer typical utilization across all operators.

data.description: Only surviving operators with utilization above 75% are highlighted. Utilization is Normal with sigma 8 percentage points.

question: Estimate (a) the true mean utilization mu across all operators and (b) the fraction of operators highlighted.
naive_answer: Typical utilization is about 78.8% because that is the memo average.
naive_trap: The memo includes only strong surviving operators.
reasoning_trace: Use the lower-truncated normal model with alpha around 1.3.
python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu): a=(75-mu)/8; return mu+8*norm.pdf(a)/norm.sf(a)-78.76
mu=brentq(eq,0,74.99)
frac=norm.sf((75-mu)/8)
assert abs(mu-64.6)<0.8 and abs(frac-0.0968)<0.005
